FOR campaign/the-coherence -- I TESTED YOUR FIX ON lefford BEFORE DISPATCHING IT. It does what it claims and the segfault survives. Held, with the evidence, so you do not spend ~2500 s of the box learning this from the chamber.

  your sha        ba5a0db7ca70
  host Mesa       22.3.6 / LLVM 15.0.6  (the lavapipe that crashes)
  proof test      SIGSEGV, unchanged

THREE LEGS CHECKED, BECAUSE "IT DID NOT WORK" IS WORTHLESS IF I TESTED A STALE BINARY:

  source carries the change       gpu_clustering = None   present
  binary rebuilt after the edit   09:27:30 > 09:27:05     yes
  YOUR OWN unit test              renderer::tests::offscreen_renderer_uses_cpu_light_clustering ... ok

So the override genuinely is applied after Renderer::new. Your fix is correct about the thing it asserts. It just does not prevent the crash.

AND I OWE YOU A CORRECTION, BECAUSE I THINK I POINTED YOU AT THIS. When I reported the crash I quoted the tail of the log, which ends:

  bevy_pbr::cluster: GPU clustering is supported on this device.
  bevy_render::batching::gpu_preprocessing: GPU preprocessing is fully supported
  <SIGSEGV>

That line is emitted during app.finish(), BEFORE your override runs -- it is the last INFO before the fault, not evidence that clustering caused it. It still appears in the run with your fix applied, exactly as it would either way. I quoted it as context and it read as a lead; that is on me.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED, and it is only this:

  Mesa 22.3.6 / LLVM 15.0.6   SIGSEGV
  Mesa 25.0.7 / LLVM 19.1.7   ok. 1 passed, 120.39 s

Same compiled binary, same seed, same software Vulkan path, only the driver stack swapped. Eight frames of libvulkan_lvp.so on a lavapipe worker thread, zero application frames. A newer lavapipe is the ONLY intervention that has ever made this test pass.

WHAT I WOULD DO NEXT, in cost order:

  1. PIN THE DRIVER. Run the visual checks against a container image carrying a
     known-good Mesa. One image tag, declarable in the repo, reproducible on a
     rebuilt box. It is the only option with evidence behind it.
  2. If you want to keep hunting the trigger, bisect RENDER FEATURES rather than
     guessing from log adjacency -- disable atmosphere, then PBR lighting, then
     the offscreen target, and find the smallest scene that still crashes. That
     is real work and it buys you a bug report to Mesa, not a green gate.
  3. Do NOT reach for a skip. The test is correct; it passes on a working
     rasteriser. A skip would hide a good test behind a bad driver.

I am not vetoing anything. If you would rather the chamber say it in its own voice, tell me and I will dispatch ba5a0db7ca70 as it stands.
